attributes.title: Level 1

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓Did you edit the number in the [change life by] block in the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Why should the Player sprite lose a life when it overlaps with an Enemy sprite?

❓ What happens when the [change life by] variable is a number greater than zero? What happens when it’s a number less than zero?


Solution:

The number in the [change life by] bubble should be changed from 3 to -1.
steps.instructions:
When the bat sprite overlaps with the tree sprite, the bat gains too many lives, too quickly.


Fix the bugs in the code so the bat sprite loses one life when it overlaps with the tree sprite.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


In this game, the bat is flying through the night and needs to avoid the trees until the time runs out!

validationItems.failureText: Edit the code so that the bat sprite loses a life after it overlaps with the tree sprite.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ Did you try out different time length parameters in the white bubble of the [start countdown] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ How long should the countdown last in this game? 

❓What number should you use so that the game is not too long, but also not too short?


Solution: 

The time parameter in the white bubble of the [start countdown] block should be replaced with a larger number, between 10 and 30, so that the game goes on for a longer period of time.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the countdown ends too quickly to play the game!


Fix the bug in the code so the bat sprite has more time to dodge the trees.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


In this game, the bat is flying through the night and needs to avoid the trees until the time runs out!

validationItems.failureText: Check the time parameter in the [start countdown] block.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Did you change the toggle on the  [game over] block in the [on countdown end] container block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓Is the toggle on the [game over] block set correctly? 

❓What else might cause the game to end in a win or lose?


Solution: 

In the [on countdown end] container, the toggle on the [game over] block should be switched from “LOSE” to “WIN.”
steps.instructions:
When the countdown ends and the bat sprite still has lives left, the game ends in a lose!


Fix the bug in the code so that the game ends in a win when the countdown ends.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


In this game, the bat is flying through the night and needs to avoid the trees until the time runs out!

validationItems.failureText: Check that the toggle is set to the “WIN” position in the [game over] block.

attributes.description: Welcome to Level 1 of Yellow Belt! In this level, you’ll learn about variables, which are pieces of data that can be stored, updated, and used in your programs. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 1:

badges.title: Data Entry
badges.description: Use variables to keep track of data in a project.

badges.title: YOLO
badges.description: Set and change the lives variable in a project.

badges.title: Time Flies
badges.description: Set a countdown timer in a project.

badges.title: Keeping Track
badges.description: Set and change the score variable in a project.

badges.title: -poof-
badges.description: Destroy a sprite when something happens in a project.
